title: I was going to call you
goal: Talk about plans in the past, and what became of them, with -jAkdY.

intro.text: Add `-dY` and the past endings to the future `-jAk`: *Saňa jaň etjekdim, ýöne wagtym bolmady*, I was going to call you, but I didn't have time. **Wasn't going to**: *gitjek däldim*. **Were you going to?**: *geljekmidiň?*

vocab.en: to fall ill, to get sick

exercises.question: How do you say **I was going to call you**?

why.1: *jaň etjek* is the future, **will call**, and it would need its subject: *Men saňa jaň etjek*.

exercises.explain: `-jAk` + `-dY` + *-m*: *jaň etjekdim*, I was going to call.

exercises.label: *gitmek* with `-jAkdY`: I was going to go…
exercises.explain: *gitjek* + *-di* + the past endings. Before *-jek*, a consonant, *git-* keeps its *t*.

exercises.text: Biz düýn Mara git___, ýöne otly gelmedi.
exercises.en: We were going to go to Mary yesterday, but the train didn't come.

reject.why: *gitjek* alone is the future. For a plan in the past: *gitjekdik*.
*gitdik* says **we went**, but the train didn't come. For the plan: *gitjekdik*.

exercises.prompt: Men saňa hat ýazjakdym, ýöne ýatdan çykardym.
accept: I was going to write you a letter, but I forgot.
I was going to write to you, but I forgot.
I meant to write you a letter, but I forgot.
I was going to write a letter to you, but I forgot.

exercises.prompt: I was going to call you, but I didn't have time.
accept: Men saňa jaň etjekdim, ýöne wagtym bolmady.
Saňa jaň etjekdim, ýöne wagtym bolmady.
(Men) size jaň etjekdim, ýöne wagtym bolmady.

reject.answer: Men saňa jaň etjek, ýöne wagtym bolmady.
reject.why: *jaň etjek* is the future. For a plan in the past that didn't happen: *jaň etjekdim*.

exercises.explain: *jaň etjekdim*, I was going to call; *wagtym bolmady*, I didn't have time.

exercises.question: Why didn't Merdan go to the wedding?

context.tk: Sen düýn toýa näme üçin gelmediň?
context.en: Why didn't you come to the wedding yesterday?

context.tk: Aslynda men geljekdim. Ýöne kakam kesel boldy.
context.en: Actually, I was going to come. But my father fell ill.

why.1: He says the opposite: *Aslynda men geljekdim*, actually I was going to come.
why.2: Nothing was forgotten: *kakam kesel boldy*, my father fell ill.

exercises.explain: *Aslynda men geljekdim. Ýöne kakam kesel boldy.*

reject.why: *geljekmi?* asks about the future, **will you come?** For **were you going to?**: *geljekmidiň?*

accept: I was just going to call you!
I was just about to call you!
I was going to call you just now!
I was about to call you just now!

exercises.text: Men gitjek ___, ýöne dostum meni çagyrdy.
exercises.en: I wasn't going to go, but my friend invited me.
exercises.explain: *däl* takes `-dY` and the ending: *gitjek däldim*, I wasn't going to go.

exercises.prompt: Actually, we were going to stay at home.
We were going to meet at the café, but it was closed.
accept: Biz kafede duşuşjakdyk, ýöne ol ýapykdy.

reject.answer: Biz kafede duşuşjak, ýöne ol ýapykdy.
reject.why: *duşuşjak* is the future. For a plan in the past: *duşuşjakdyk*.

exercises.explain: *duşuşjakdyk*, we were going to meet; *ýapykdy*, it was closed.

exercises.label: *gelmek* with `-jAkdY`, negative: I wasn't going to come…
exercises.explain: *däl* after *geljek* takes `-dY` and the ending: *geljek däldim*. *gelmejekdim* is also used.
